description: Dubu Jorim is a beloved Korean vegetarian dish featuring pan-fried tofu simmered in a rich, spicy, and savory braising sauce. This comforting and flavorful meal is incredibly satisfying, offering a delightful balance of textures and bold Korean flavors. It's a perfect hearty option for a plant-based dinner that truly warms the soul.

instructions.title: Prepare and Pan-Fry Tofu
instructions.text: Press the tofu blocks for at least 30 minutes to remove excess water, then slice each block into 8-10 rectangular pieces. Heat vegetable oil in a large non-stick pan over medium-high heat. Carefully add the tofu slices in a single layer and pan-fry for 3-5 minutes per side until golden brown and slightly crispy. Remove fried tofu and set aside on a plate lined with paper towels.

instructions.title: Prepare the Braising Sauce
instructions.text: In a medium bowl, combine the soy sauce, gochugaru, gochujang, minced garlic, 2 chopped green onions, sugar or maple syrup, sesame oil, and water or vegetable broth. Whisk all ingredients together until well combined and the gochujang is fully dissolved. Taste and adjust seasoning if necessary, adding more gochugaru for extra spice or sugar for sweetness.

instructions.title: Arrange Tofu for Braising
instructions.text: In a large shallow pot or a deep skillet, carefully arrange the pan-fried tofu slices in a single layer. Try not to overlap them too much to ensure even cooking and sauce distribution. If your pan is small, you might need to layer them slightly or use a wider pan.

instructions.title: Simmer the Tofu in Sauce
instructions.text: Pour the prepared braising sauce evenly over the arranged tofu slices. Bring the sauce to a gentle simmer over medium heat. Once simmering, reduce the heat to low, cover the pot, and let it braise for 20 minutes, allowing the tofu to absorb the rich flavors of the sauce.

instructions.title: Reduce and Thicken the Sauce
instructions.text: After 20 minutes, remove the lid. Gently spoon some of the sauce over the tofu pieces to ensure they are thoroughly coated. Continue to simmer uncovered for another 5-10 minutes, or until the sauce has slightly thickened to your desired consistency. Be careful not to stir too vigorously to avoid breaking the tofu.

instructions.title: Garnish and Serve
instructions.text: Remove the Dubu Jorim from the heat. Garnish generously with the remaining chopped green onion and a sprinkle of toasted sesame seeds. Serve immediately with a bowl of freshly cooked rice and other Korean side dishes like kimchi or pickled radishes.

tips: To achieve perfectly crispy tofu, ensure you press out as much water as possible before frying. You can use a tofu press or wrap it in paper towels and place a heavy object on top for 30-60 minutes.
Adjust the spice level by increasing or decreasing the amount of gochugaru. For a milder version, you can reduce it to 1 tablespoon or omit the gochujang.

Dubu Jorim tastes even better the next day as the flavors meld further. Store leftovers in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3-4 days. Reheat gently on the stovetop or in the microwave.
